page.title: Live session
page.purpose: Operate a device under an explicit lease, with the holder, the expiry, and the kill control always visible.

priorities.statement: The lease holder, its expiry, and a one-click kill are always visible while the session is live.
priorities.notes: A live control session on a personal device must never be discoverable only by navigating to it.

priorities.statement: Every control is operable and every state perceivable without the video frame.
priorities.notes: The frame is evidence, not the interface. It is also absent entirely on strategies whose transport cannot stream.

priorities.statement: Each dispatched verb appears in a running audit list with its outcome.
priorities.notes: The audit is the accountability record; a verb that executed without a visible entry is unaccounted for.

states.description: A live session with a held lease and a streaming frame.
The lease request is in flight; no controls are enabled yet.
No lease has been acquired yet; the page explains what acquiring one will do and who else may currently hold it.
The session is live but a declared capability is unavailable, so some controls are absent with a stated reason rather than inert.
The frame stream has stopped advancing while the lease remains held; the last frame is labelled with its age rather than presented as live.
A dispatched verb failed at the transport. The session survives and the failure is recorded in the audit list.
Lease acquisition in progress; controls remain disabled until it is held.
Another consumer holds the lease. The refusal names the holder and the expiry rather than queueing silently.
The strategy cannot supply a frame. Every control and the semantic tree remain fully operable.
The lease is close to expiry; renewal is offered before control is lost mid-action.
The session was terminated. Controls are gone, the audit list is retained, and the reason for termination is stated.

elements.name: Lease held
elements.description: Holder, elapsed time, and expiry countdown. Occupies the same position as on every other route.

elements.name: Kill session
elements.description: Immediate termination, styled as destructive and never behind a menu.

elements.name: Renew
elements.description: Extends the lease before expiry interrupts an action in progress.

elements.name: Screen
elements.description: The live frame pane. Evidence rather than interface — hiding it must not reduce operability.
Capture method and effective frame rate, so a synthesized reconstruction is never mistaken for a native stream.

elements.name: Semantic tree
elements.description: Addressable element hierarchy for deterministic targeting. Present only when the strategy declares semantic-tree.
Which rung the current targeting is using — semantic, visual-anchor, or vision — and its confidence.

elements.name: Dispatch
elements.description: Tap, type, swipe, key, and navigation verbs. The complete control surface independent of the frame.

elements.name: Verb audit
elements.description: Append-only list of dispatched verbs with timing and outcome.
Names the current holder and expiry when a lease claim is refused.
Explains why a control is absent on this strategy rather than rendering it disabled.

claims.statement: While a lease is held, the holder and its expiry are perceivable at all times.
claims.rationale: Priority 1 and D-006. This is the scenario's central safety property.

claims.statement: The kill control is reachable without scrolling for the entire duration of a live session.
claims.rationale: A safety control below the fold is not a safety control.

claims.statement: The kill control is operable from the keyboard throughout a live session.
claims.rationale: SECURITY.md requires kill to be one action away; a pointer-only control fails that for keyboard and assistive-technology users alike.

claims.statement: With no frame available, the dispatch controls and the verb audit remain present and operable.
claims.rationale: Priority 2. This is simultaneously the accessibility floor and what keeps a frameless transport usable.

claims.statement: The frame-unavailable state renders a stated explanation rather than a blank pane.
claims.rationale: A blank region reads as a broken stream; the truth is that this transport has no stream.

claims.statement: Whenever a frame is shown, its capture method and effective frame rate are shown with it.
claims.rationale: D-009. A synthesized low-rate reconstruction and a native capture support different claims and must never look identical.

claims.statement: A frame that has stopped advancing is perceivably different from a live one.
claims.rationale: Acting on a stale frame is how an operator taps the wrong thing. The difference must be visible before the tap.

claims.statement: Each dispatched verb appears in the audit list with its outcome, including failures.
claims.rationale: Priority 3 and DVC-P0-009. A verb with no visible entry is unaccounted for.

claims.statement: A refused lease claim states who holds the device and when it expires, rather than failing generically.
claims.rationale: D-006 refuses rather than queues, so the refusal has to carry enough information for the operator to decide what to do next.

claims.statement: A control unavailable on this strategy is explained rather than rendered as an inert button.
claims.rationale: A disabled control invites repeated clicking and implies a temporary condition; unsupported is terminal on that transport.

claims.statement: The resolution rung in use, and its confidence, are perceivable while targeting.
claims.rationale: D-004. A reviewer must be able to tell a deterministic match from an inferred one at the moment it happens, not only afterwards.

claims.statement: After termination the verb audit remains readable and the reason for termination is stated.
claims.rationale: Killing a session must not destroy the accountability record it produced.
